qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global marine service and OEM parts footprint across 200+ ports; pricing power demonstrated in long-term marine lifecycle service agreements and dual-fuel engine systems, though energy storage faces fierce price competition.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Peak-to-Peak Compounding, REJECT). While marine lifecycle service agreements and OEM spare parts generate strong cash conversion and a net cash balance sheet, long-term earnings power is hostage to violent global shipbuilding and shipyard order cycles, alongside structural price competition and margin drag in grid battery energy storage.
qualitative.evidence: Marine and Energy operating results have historically swung with shipyard newbuild cycles (e.g. multi-year post-2008 depression in ship orders). Energy storage division operates at thin/volatile margins under heavy competition from Chinese battery integrators, undermining repeatable peak-to-peak business cycle compounding.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
